records.current_summary: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier: no union-territory-specific trans law, enforcement series or incident pattern was found, and (not among the 12 states/UTs that constituted the mandated welfare board) its protective policy depends on the Union government, an RTI-documented driver of the welfare-board gap. No deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); assessed at the national score.

sources.claim: HRW report (26 Mar 2026): India's parliament passed the 2026 Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill narrowing the 2019 law: it removes self-identification, restricts legal recognition to traditionally recognised groups (hijra/kinner) and intersex persons, and requires medical certification for identity recognition — reversing the 2014 Supreme Court ruling. The bill adds offences including up to life imprisonment for 'coercing or alluring' anyone to be transgender, which HRW warns could criminalise support networks. Of 487,803 census-recorded transgender persons, only about 32,500 hold identity cards. HRW urges the president not to sign; assent pending as of late March 2026.

BBC (26 Mar 2026): India's parliament passed an amendment to the 2019 transgender-rights law replacing self-identification with recognition based on biological or physical traits plus traditional identities (hijra/kinner-style); medical boards and district authorities must now certify gender-affirming surgery. The government says the narrower definition targets welfare benefits and anti-trafficking protection; critics warn it excludes many trans men, trans women and non-binary people. A Supreme Court-appointed advisory panel asked the government to withdraw the bill, calling removal of self-identification a setback against the 2014 ruling; presidential assent is pending. India is estimated to have around two million transgender people.

records.name: Madhya Pradesh
records.current_summary: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which found no Madhya Pradesh-specific trans statute or enforcement series and records it among the states/UTs that have not constituted the mandated transgender welfare board; with national legal uniformity (no state criminalisation) the deviation was not material enough to score separately (±0.02), so it is assessed at the national score.

sources.claim: National-framework item (applies to Madhya Pradesh): India's parliament passed the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill on 25 March 2026 amid protests in Mumbai. If assented, it removes the 2014 self-identification right, limits legal recognition to historically accepted categories (traditional communities and intersex people), mandates medical certification, and adds offences carrying up to life imprisonment for 'coercing or alluring' people to be transgender — amending the 2019 law. The rights group People's Union for Civil Liberties warns the offences echo colonial-era criminalisation of transgender people.

National-framework item (applies to Madhya Pradesh): BBC coverage of the same bill India's parliament passed in March 2026, approved by both houses and awaiting presidential assent. It ends the 2014 Supreme Court self-identification right, narrows recognition to male/female categories plus traditional identities, and makes medical-board and district-authority certification mandatory for gender-affirming surgery. Critics warn the narrower definition excludes self-identifying gender-fluid and non-binary people; ~2 million transgender people live in India.

records.name: Goa
records.current_summary:
The country dossier found no divergent Goan trans statute or enforcement pattern: the national framework alone defines Goa's legal position. In March 2026 that framework narrowed sharply — both houses removed the 2014 self-identification right, restricted legal recognition to traditional-community and intersex categories with mandatory medical certification, and added a coercion offence carrying up to life imprisonment, drawing a withdrawal request from a court-appointed advisory panel, protests after the vote, and warnings of exclusion from named trans activists; presidential assent was pending.

Neither the human-rights nor broadcast reporting on the change records any Goan ordinance, welfare-board action or incident series deviating in either direction: recognition machinery, certification boards and the new offence operate in Goa exactly as in every other state and territory, and that uniformity is the whole of the documented local picture.

records.name: Chandīgarh
records.current_summary: This union territory was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); it is therefore assessed at the national score. Its one unit-level signal is official-will positive: Chandīgarh is among only 12 of India's 36 states/UTs that have constituted the transgender welfare board required by the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Rules, 2020 — though an RTI investigation found most such boards rudderless, without a policy framework, compliance mechanism or real power.

records.name: Jammu and Kashmīr
records.current_summary: No region-specific trans law or enforcement series was located in the research pass; the unit's distinction is structural rather than legislative. In 2019 the former state was reconstituted as a union territory governed by an appointed Administrator without a legislature, and armed-forces jurisdiction under AFSPA persists in parts — a heavy checkpoint-and-document regime that raises appearance-and-identity scrutiny for every traveller, and therefore specifically for anyone whose documents and presentation differ.
